purpose: Bind video architecture and product recommendations to explicit evidence and certification gates.

evidence.scope: One staging L40S; H.264 1280x720 at native 60 FPS; YOLOv8 Nano; output disabled; one worker; threaded A/B/C runtimes.

facts.interpretation: C improved aggregate throughput above the strict knee without increasing the strict low-latency concurrency boundary. The first C failure was not whole-pod, relay, GPU, VRAM, or decoder saturation.

evidence.scope: A c1 source-rate-limiter validity gate, not a packing curve.

facts.interpretation: The maxFps path can attain its c1 target after the limiter flag change; controlled multi-stream capacity remains unmeasured.

evidence.scope: Credential-free image/import/spawn smokes for D/E/F only.
D/E/F c1/c2 topology, selective cancellation, child crash, cleanup, then repeated capacity curves.
Historical Burstable CPU worker; YOLOv8 Nano; output disabled; mutable image evidence.
Guaranteed cpu-2/cpu-4/cpu-8 classes; thread/process; 5/8/10/15 FPS; light/heavy mixes; matched telemetry.
Matched output off/on plus detection, tracking, dual-model, and segmentation arrivals.
Balanced, delayed-arrival, heavy-neighbor, reverse-order, and output-noise runs across two staging workspaces.
Single-workspace MMP smoke and legacy/direct/subprocess controls at 4K and 640p.

facts.interpretation: The 4K subprocess regression disappeared in the 640p control, implicating ndarray shared-memory transport rather than proving a production manager topology.

evidence.scope: Per-job authorization, warm-model denial, result/slot separation, fair queues, backend failure, and tenant accounting.
Exclusive L40S MMP comparison with MPS off/on and optional thread caps; throughput, latency, fairness, and faults.
Startup loss, steady processor loss, relay replacement, exact pod identity, and verified post-replacement frame progress.
Sticky source home cell, cell-scoped job claims, explicit remote execution, relay shards, and dedicated placement policies.
Isolated LB, relay, CNI, node, cross-cell, cloud, and on-prem edges with source/fan-out curves.
Worker, relay, bandwidth, control-plane, and failure-overhead cost inputs joined to successful service units.

currentRecommendation.action: Use one OS process per job as the leading isolation and scaling candidate, but do not select it for deployment until D/E/F lifecycle and capacity gates pass.
currentRecommendation.scope: GPU stream jobs; decoder, workflow, model, CUDA context, and publisher stay in the child; frames and tensors do not cross supervisor IPC.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: The image smokes do not prove selective cancellation, crash containment, capacity, security isolation, or a production worker class.

certificationRequirements.requirement: At c2, the supervisor and both jobs have distinct PIDs and the runtime identity matches the exact D/E/F digest.
Cancel or kill one child without interrupting sibling frame progress; sanitize the failure and return activeJobs to zero.
Run repeated, identical D/E/F curves through the first repeated failure and compare strict capacity, latency, resources, startup, and cleanup with A/B/C.
The selected topology passes the staged soak progression without process, memory, CUDA, counter, or publisher drift.

unknowns: Whether per-job processes move the c2 strict native-rate knee.
The independent-CUDA-context cost before MPS or a shared model manager.
Whether process cleanup remains bounded during model load and output publication.

currentRecommendation.action: Treat c2 as the strict maximum only for the measured native-rate 720p YOLO output-off A/B/C profiles; keep the product packing limit unknown.
currentRecommendation.scope: One L40S, one worker, native 60 FPS connector stream, strict p95 50 ms and p99 150 ms gates.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: Do not generalize c2 to 5/10/15 FPS service tiers, other resolutions, output publishing, heavy workflows, MMP, or long-lived operation.

certificationRequirements.requirement: For the exact native-rate A/B/C profile, two repetitions pass at the selected point and two higher points show the repeated SLO boundary.
Run separately labeled 5/10/15 FPS curves with c1 target attainment, two repetitions, histogram latency, resource coverage, and an observed failing boundary.
Measure matched output off/on and light, tracking, dual-model, and segmentation profiles before assigning resource units.
The proposed operating point passes soak and recovery gates with explicit headroom below the observed knee.

unknowns: Maximum strict streams at each controlled FPS and resolution.
Safe operating headroom after long soaks.
Output publishing and heavy-workflow capacity multipliers.
An independently re-runnable sanitized evidence bundle for the committed A/B/C summary.

currentRecommendation.action: Keep routing experimental. Compare Guaranteed CPU classes with the matching GPU workload before selecting CPU, GPU, or multiple CPU shapes.
currentRecommendation.scope: Routing by workflow fingerprint, model, resolution, target FPS, output mode, SLO, and measured cost—not by model family name alone.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: The historical CPU curve cannot certify current sizing, and faster GPU inference alone does not prove lower service cost.

certificationRequirements.requirement: Each candidate CPU class/topology has immutable-image repeated curves, Guaranteed QoS, CFS/resource evidence, PID identity, cleanup, and a failing boundary.
The exact workflow, model, source, FPS, output mode, SLO, and duration are measured on the candidate GPU topology.
Compare successful stream-hours and successful frames per worker-hour, plus relay/bandwidth and idle/headroom costs.

unknowns: Whether one, several, or no general CPU classes are economical.
CPU viability for tracking, dual-model, and segmentation workflows.
The utilization and queue thresholds for switching tiers.

currentRecommendation.action: A pod-global trusted model service may share model backends across jobs and workspaces; preserve per-job authorization, identity, accounting, and result routing instead of creating a manager merely because a workspace differs.
currentRecommendation.scope: Trusted service boundary inside one GPU-owning worker pod; one OS process per video job remains the pipeline isolation target.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: Trusted does not mean authorization-free, fair, memory-isolated, or fault-isolated; current single-workspace controls do not certify cross-workspace sharing.

certificationRequirements.requirement: Every job is authorized before route/cache reuse; an unauthorized tenant cannot invoke a model warmed by another tenant.
Watermarked cross-workspace traffic proves SHM slots, responses, cancellation, errors, and output paths never cross client identities.
Bounded per-client inflight work or fair queuing prevents a high-rate producer from dominating, with per-job/workspace usage attribution.
Same-model batching, different-model backends, backend death/reload, cancellation, SHM pressure, and long-lived churn pass the selected SLO.

unknowns: The winning transport and tensor descriptor between job processes and the manager.
Whether shared same-model auto-batching improves low-latency stream capacity at bounded batch wait.
The right queue isolation granularity: job, priority class, workspace policy, or a combination.

currentRecommendation.action: Make the job the execution and runtime-fairness unit. Use workspace identity only for authorization, quota, reserved/dedicated capacity, admission ordering, accounting, and reporting policy.
currentRecommendation.scope: Resource-aware worker fit plus optional weighted workspace admission; oldest eligible job selection within a workspace.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: Workspace fairness does not require a workspace process or model manager, and admission fairness does not guarantee GPU time isolation after colocation.

certificationRequirements.requirement: Every planned job is stable, reaches at least 90% of target, has histogram p95 at most 50 ms, has no counter reset/migration, and retains exact identity.
Balanced and reverse-order runs keep tenant target-attainment spread at most 10% and delayed incumbents retain at least 90%.
Tracking, segmentation, dual-model, and output arrivals do not breach incumbent SLO; otherwise admission prevents the unsafe fit.
Replay bursty multi-workspace arrivals against proposed quotas, priorities, reservations, and queue ordering without starvation or reserved-capacity spill.

unknowns: Resource-unit weights for each workflow profile.
Whether runtime interference needs manager-level per-client scheduling beyond admission control.
Product quota, priority, and reservation values.

currentRecommendation.action: Use lazy, sticky source home-cell placement and colocate ordinary live processing; let workspace/connector policy constrain or prefer cells, including strict dedicated cells with no silent shared fallback.
currentRecommendation.scope: Design direction for a second non-production cell; remote execution must be explicit and encoded-media based.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: The RFC is not runtime proof. A second cell is unsafe until source placement, URL resolution, Pub/Sub filters, and transactional claims agree on cell identity.

certificationRequirements.requirement: With one registered cell, placement is persisted, URLs are placement-derived, claims filter by verified cell, and a synthetic other-cell worker cannot claim East work.
Two staging cells prove deterministic first activation, sticky reuse, strict workspace pinning, draining, idle reassignment, and no cross-cell misclaims.
Colocated, direct remote, and one-copy-plus-local-fanout paths have measured latency, loss, recovery, capacity, egress cost, and security envelopes.
Dedicated relay/compute modes specify reservation, upgrade, draining, secret rotation, support, billing, and explicit fallback semantics.

unknowns: The first second-cell location and secure WAN transport.
Relay shard size and cell ingress/egress admission thresholds.
Which dedicated placement modes become product commitments.

currentRecommendation.action: Test raw MPS only as an optional throughput/fairness scheduler inside one exclusive L40S pod; keep it off by default until it wins repeated capacity and fault gates.
currentRecommendation.scope: MPS off versus on, same-model versus different-model processes, and optional 50%/25% active-thread caps.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: MPS is not an authorization, memory-isolation, workspace-isolation, or fault-isolation boundary. L40S does not offer MIG for this campaign.

certificationRequirements.requirement: Warm/cold/cache order, workload, process topology, target FPS, and manager settings are identical with MPS off/on through repeated failing boundaries.
Any throughput gain preserves per-job target attainment, p95/p99 latency, bounded batch wait, startup, and incumbent fairness.
Client termination, backend failure, GPU fault, MPS server fault, cleanup, and restart produce a documented blast radius and bounded recovery.
The winning MPS and non-MPS configurations pass at least a 15-minute comparison and the selected configuration passes the full soak progression.

unknowns: Whether MPS improves low-latency throughput for the actual kernel mix.
Whether active-thread caps help fairness or merely reduce utilization.
The operational impact of a fatal client or MPS server fault.

currentRecommendation.action: Keep zero recovery tolerance in capacity certification and measure faults in separate suites; advance soaks only after each shorter gate passes.
currentRecommendation.scope: Per-job child, worker pod, relay, model backend, MPS server, and long-lived resource/counter stability.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: A requeued job or replacement relay alone does not prove media continuity, state continuity, or bounded end-to-end downtime.

certificationRequirements.requirement: Exact old/new processor pod identities join fault time to verified post-replacement frame progress for startup and steady faults.
Frame identity, stalls, reconnects, and output continuity—not relay liveness alone—bound relay replacement impact.
15-minute, 1-hour, 4-hour, and 12-hour gates pass sequentially with resource series, latency tails, reconnects, restarts, reloads, and counter continuity.

unknowns: Exact frame-recovery and media-continuity bounds.
Whether stateful workflows can resume without semantic state loss.
Memory, VRAM, SHM, descriptor, and model-cache drift over 12 hours.

currentRecommendation.action: Characterize each network edge independently, then the combined cell; shard MediaMTX origins by source only after the measured relay/node/LB knee requires it.
currentRecommendation.scope: Publish, read, fan-out, output, preview, LB, CNI, node NIC, WAN, and one-copy remote fan-out paths.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: Do not call the first plateau a MediaMTX limit unless generators, node VPC entitlement, LB, CNI, CPU, and readers are all shown to have headroom.

certificationRequirements.requirement: Publish-copy, read-copy, and decode-validation isolate LB, same-node, CNI cross-node, relay-node, and processor-node edges with byte conservation.
Source and readers-per-source ramps identify the first saturated resource, a failing boundary, and a lower operating point for each fixture.
Combined processor, relay, output, and viewer runs produce the cell envelope; isolated maxima are not multiplied.

unknowns: MediaMTX process, relay-node, CNI, and Crusoe LB knees.
Safe relay shard size and reconnection rate.
Cross-cell direct-read versus one-copy local fan-out tradeoff.

currentRecommendation.action: Separate capacity allocation from customer pricing. Evaluate a managed per-stream quote pinned to workflow version and declared service envelope against an explicitly named worker-class launch step; keep worker selection platform-recommended in either case.
currentRecommendation.scope: Worker, relay, bandwidth, idle/ready headroom, retry/failure overhead, output, and dedicated reservations.
currentRecommendation.doNotClaim: Throughput, admission ceiling, GPU utilization, or the product-discussion c15 break-even hypothesis is not a price and must not weaken the SLO.

certificationRequirements.requirement: Define successful stream-hours and successful processed frames using target attainment, latency, availability, and error gates; exclude failed/requeued time from delivered service.
Supply worker-hour, relay, bandwidth/egress, control-plane, ready-capacity, and dedicated-reservation costs for the measured environment.
Compute cost per successful stream-hour and successful frame by versioned workload profile at the certified operating point and headroom.

Product review selects managed per-stream versus worker-class packaging, workflow-edit repricing, under-provision behavior, margins, quotas, reservations, and overages independently from the measured capacity calculation.

unknowns: Actual environment and egress costs.
The customer-facing billing unit and included FPS/resolution/output envelope.
Whether worker classes are only an internal allocator, a launch-step customer contract, or both.
Margins and reserved/dedicated capacity commitments.
